1	---
2	title: "Tools: projects and history"
3	description: The agent tools that open, make, save, close and read a project, and walk its undo history, with every argument, answer and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools work on whole projects: opening, making, saving and closing them, reading one back, and stepping through its undo history. None of them takes `scope`, because none of them edits inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'save_project', 'close_project', 'get_project', 'undo', 'redo']}
12	/>
13	
14	Every tool takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. A path that names no open project is refused, and so is a call with no project open at all, which is told to call `open_project` or `new_project` first. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/) for how times are written, and [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the short `project` summary most answers carry.
15	
16	## `open_project`
17	
18	Opens a project and shows its window, as [double-clicking a file](/projects/open-a-project/) does. It takes a `.framejob` package, or any movie, sound file or picture. A movie, sound file or picture [becomes a new untitled project](/projects/start-a-project/) sized and rated to it, with the file as the first clip on track 1.
19	
20	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
22	| `path` | string | Yes | The file to open, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
23	| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |
24	
25	It answers the opened project's `project` summary, with `missing_media` in that summary when a file has gone. If the file is already open, Frame Job brings that project forward and answers `already_open: true` with its summary. That includes a movie already open as an untitled project.
26	
27	It's refused when:
28	
29	- nothing exists at `path`
30	- the file can't be read, or doesn't open as a Frame Job project
31	- you're opening the same file in a window and that open hasn't finished after 30 seconds. Call it again once the window is up.
32	
33	A tool call never asks a question, so a file that would normally bring up the [ffmpeg offer](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) is treated as if you'd declined it.
34	
35	## `new_project`
36	
37	Makes a blank 1920×1080, 30 fps project and shows its window, as [**File ▸ New Project**](/projects/start-a-project/#start-a-blank-project) does. Change its size and rate afterwards with [`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
38	
39	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
40	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
41	| `path` | string | No | Where to save it straight away, such as `~/Movies/Cut.framejob`. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Without a path the project stays an untitled draft until `save_project`. |
42	| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |
43	
44	It answers the new project's `project` summary, and `saved`, the full path, when you gave one.
45	
46	A path another open project holds is refused and nothing is created. `close_project` closes that project first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced.
47	
48	## `new_project_from_range`
49	
50	Opens a stretch of the top-level timeline as a new project, moved to start at 0, as [**File ▸ New Project from Range…**](/projects/new-project-from-range/) does with the in/out range. The project you take it from doesn't change and gets no undo step.
51	
52	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
53	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
54	| `from` | integer | Yes | Where the range starts on the timeline, in ticks. It's rounded to a frame, and a negative time is taken as 0. |
55	| `to` | integer | Yes | Where the range ends on the timeline, in ticks. The frame at `to` isn't kept. It must be after `from`. |
56	| `path` | string | No | Where to save the new project first. `.framejob` is added when it's missing, and nothing may exist there yet. Without it the project opens untitled, with unsaved changes, named "*name* (range)". |
57	| `project` | string | No | The project to take the range from. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
58	
59	What's kept follows the sheet:
60	
61	- A clip across an edge is cut there, on every track, as [`split`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/) would cut it. Locked tracks are cut too.
62	- A transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end.
63	- Markers inside the range are kept and moved with it.
64	- Media nothing kept plays is left out.
65	- Each kept file's caches come along, so nothing is analysed again, and so do the graphics the kept clips draw, with every font and picture. [What comes with it](/projects/new-project-from-range/#what-comes-with-it) has the list.
66	- Media files are never copied. The new project points at the same files.
67	
68	It answers `project`, the new project's summary, `carried` with the `files`, `bytes` and `seconds` that came along, and `saved`, the path, when you gave one. The new project opens in front, so later calls with no `project` reach it. Name it by its path once it has one.
69	
70	It's refused:
71	
72	- while a nest is open. Call `set_scope` with no arguments first.
73	- when `to` isn't after `from`, once both are on the frame grid
74	- for a path another open project holds, or where anything already exists
75	- for a nest clip across either edge, because a nest clip has no in point and would replay from its start
76	- when nothing plays in the range
77	- when an edge would leave a transition inside the range too long for what's left of its clip. Move that edge further from the transition.
78	
79	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first when the call names a `path`.
80	
81	## `save_project`
82	
83	Saves the project, as [**File ▸ Save**](/projects/save-and-revert/#save-a-project) does, and answers only once the package is on disk.
84	
85	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
86	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
87	| `path` | string | The first time | Where to write the `.framejob` package. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Giving a path always writes there, as Save As does, unless it's the project's own file, which is a plain save. |
88	| `project` | string | No | The project to save. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
89	
90	A project needs a `path` the first time, whether it came from `new_project` with no path or from a movie opened as a project. After that, leave it out and the project is written back to its own file.
91	
92	It answers `saved`, the full path, and the `project` summary.
93	
94	It's refused when a project that has never been saved has no `path`, and for a path another open project holds. `close_project` closes that one first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced. A save that takes more than 120 seconds answers that it timed out.
95	
96	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first.
97	
98	## `close_project`
99	
100	Closes a project and its window, as [**File ▸ Close**](/projects/save-and-revert/#close-a-project) (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) does. It never writes the package, so call `save_project` first to keep your changes.
101	
102	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
103	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
104	| `discard` | boolean | No | Close even with unsaved changes, losing them. Default `false`. |
105	| `project` | string | No | The project to close. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
106	
107	It answers `ok: true`, `closed` (the project's name), `path` (null for a blank project never saved) and `discarded_changes`, which says whether unsaved changes went with it. A later call naming that path is refused, because it's no longer open.
108	
109	It's refused when the window has a sheet open, whatever `discard` says, and when `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes` and `discard` isn't `true`.
110	
111	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call this tool, because closing the project would close its own conversation.
112	
113	## `get_project`
114	
115	Answers the whole project as JSON, plus what the app holds outside it: the playhead, the selection and the in/out range. Read it first, because every other tool names things by the ids it reports. [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/) goes through it in full.
116	
117	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
118	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
119	| `project` | string | No | The project to read. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
120	
121	Its answer holds:
122	
123	| Key | What it is |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| `project` | The project itself, including `canvas`, `media`, `tracks`, `clips`, `markers`, `nests` and `next_id`. |
126	| `path`, `name` | Where the project is, or null, and what it's called. |
127	| `unsaved_changes` | Whether it has changes not yet saved. |
128	| `duration`, `playhead` | Its length and the playhead, in ticks. |
129	| `selection` | The selected clip ids. |
130	| `in_out_range` | `start` and `end`, in ticks. Only there when a range is set. |
131	| `scope` | The open nest's id, or null at the timeline. With a nest open, `scope_clip` and `scope_path` come with it. |
132	| `missing_media` | The ids of media whose file has gone. Only there when one has. |
133	| `graphics` | Every module in the package, with its revision, whether it compiles, and the clips it draws. |
134	| `note` | A reminder of how to read the rest. |
135	
136	While a nest is open, `project` is that nest seen as a project. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
137	
138	## `undo`
139	
140	Undoes one step, as [**Edit ▸ Undo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) does. Every tool that edits makes exactly one step, so one `undo` walks back exactly one call. The history is the project's, so a step you made by hand counts as well.
141	
142	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
143	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
144	| `project` | string | No | The project to undo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
145	
146	It answers `ok: true`, `undone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.
147	
148	It's refused when there's nothing to undo. The tools on [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/) make no step, so they can't be undone.
149	
150	## `redo`
151	
152	Redoes one undone step, as [**Edit ▸ Redo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) does. Any new edit clears what there was to redo, as it does in the app.
153	
154	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
155	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
156	| `project` | string | No | The project to redo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
157	
158	It answers `ok: true`, `redone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.
159	
160	It's refused when there's nothing to redo.
161

1	---
2	title: "Tools: playhead, range and selection"
3	description: The agent tools that move the playhead, set the in/out range, select clips and open a nest, none of which is an edit.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These four tools change what the app is looking at, never the project. They make no undo step and leave the project untouched, so `undo` can't reverse them. `get_project` reads all of them back.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />
11	
12	Times are in ticks, 600,000 per second, and each is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). Every tool here takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
13	
14	## `set_playhead`
15	
16	Moves the playhead and seeks the preview, as [clicking the ruler or a transport key](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) does.
17	
18	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| `t` | integer | Yes | The time to move to, in ticks. A negative time goes to 0. |
21	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
22	
23	It answers `ok: true`, `playhead` (the time it landed on) and the `project` summary.
24	
25	`split`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker` use this time when they aren't given one. While a [nest](/mcp/nests/) is open, `t` is measured from the nest's own start.
26	
27	## `set_range`
28	
29	Sets or clears the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), as **Mark ▸ Set In** (<kbd>I</kbd>), **Mark ▸ Set Out** (<kbd>O</kbd>) and **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) do.
30	
31	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| `start` | integer | No | The In point, in ticks. Left out, it keeps the range's current In, or 0 when there's no range. |
34	| `end` | integer | No | The Out point, in ticks. Left out, it keeps the range's current Out, or the project's end when there's no range. |
35	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
36	
37	Call it with neither bound to clear the range. A negative time is taken as 0.
38	
39	It answers `ok: true`, `in_out_range` (`start` and `end`, or null when the range is cleared) and the `project` summary.
40	
41	It's refused when the end isn't after the start. [`export`](/mcp/export/) with `range: "in_out"` writes only this span, and `get_project` reports it as `in_out_range`.
42	
43	## `set_selection`
44	
45	Selects clips, as [clicking one](/timeline/selecting-clips/) in the timeline or on the canvas, or **Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>), does. The canvas handles, crop mode and every inspector pane act on the selection, so this puts the app into the state you want to look at.
46	
47	You don't need it to edit. The editing tools take their own `clip` or `clips`.
48	
49	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
50	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
51	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clip ids to select, replacing the selection. Leave it out, or pass an empty array, to select nothing. |
52	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
53	
54	It answers `ok: true`, `selection` (the selected ids, in order) and the `project` summary.
55	
56	An id that isn't a clip is refused by name. With a nest open, ids mean clips inside that nest, so a clip on the timeline can't be selected until you come back out with `set_scope`.
57	
58	## `set_scope`
59	
60	Opens a nest so the app is looking inside it, or comes back out, as [double-clicking a nest clip](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest), **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>) and **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>) do.
61	
62	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
63	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
64	| `clip` | integer | No | The nest clip to open. This is the precise choice: it names the nest and the start that times inside are measured from, and it works at any depth. |
65	| `nest` | integer | No | The nest to open, by id, as `get_project` lists them under `nests`. A clip on the timeline must show it. Where two clips do, the earliest is entered, and a tie goes to the lower id. |
66	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
67	
68	Pass `clip` or `nest`, not both. Pass neither to come back out to the timeline. The call names where to be, not a step to take, so it means the same thing from any depth.
69	
70	While a nest is open:
71	
72	- `get_project` reports the nest's own tracks, clips and canvas, and [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) draws it. This is the only way to see what an edit inside a nest did.
73	- An edit lands inside the nest, unless its own `scope` says otherwise or it belongs to the whole project, as a change to the [media list](/mcp/tools-media/) does. So open the nest first, and clear it when you're done.
74	
75	Going in maps the playhead to the nest's own time and selects nothing. Coming out maps it back and selects the nest clip you opened.
76	
77	You don't need this tool to edit inside a nest. An edit tool's `scope` argument works from wherever the window is looking. [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/) covers both ways.
78	
79	It answers `ok: true`, `scope` (the nest's id, or null at the timeline), `scope_clip` and `scope_path` with a nest open, `playhead`, and the `project` summary.
80	
81	It's refused when:
82	
83	- both `clip` and `nest` are given
84	- no clip has that id, at the timeline or in any nest
85	- the clip doesn't show a nest
86	- no nest has that id
87	- no clip on the timeline shows that nest. Name the nest clip with `clip`, or send the edit with `scope`.
88

1	---
2	title: "Tools: media"
3	description: The agent tools that bring files into a project, relink and remove them, copy them into the package, and set a file's Camera Log, peak and speech.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools work on the project's media list, the files a project points at. A file on the list isn't on the timeline until a clip uses it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'consolidate_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech']}
12	/>
13	
14	The media list belongs to the whole project, not to a nest, so:
15	
16	- Pass `scope` to `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color` or `set_media_speech`, and Frame Job answers that the edit has no meaning inside a nest.
17	- With a nest open and no `scope` passed, those same edits apply to the whole project. All but `add_media` name themselves under `document_ops` in the answer.
18	- Media ids mean the same thing everywhere.
19	
20	Every tool here also takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. Each edit is one undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the `project` summary and the two ways an edit can fail to happen.
21	
22	## `import_media`
23	
24	Reads a movie, sound file, picture or `.cube` LUT and adds it to the media list, as [**File ▸ Add Media…**](/projects/import-media/#add-media) does. It isn't on the timeline yet. Place it with [`add_clip`](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/).
25	
26	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
27	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
28	| `path` | string | Yes | The file, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
29	| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
30	
31	It answers:
32	
33	| Key | What it is |
34	| --- | --- |
35	| `media` | The new media id. |
36	| `path` | Where the entry points. For a converted file, that's the copy. |
37	| `original` | The file you named, when the entry points at a copy. |
38	| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. |
39	| `duration` | The file's length, in ticks. |
40	| `width`, `height` | Its display size. |
41	| `fps` | Its frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. |
42	| `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha` | What it holds. |
43	| `note` | What to do next: `add_clip`, or for a LUT, [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/) with a look. |
44	| `project` | The `project` summary. |
45	
46	A [WebM or Matroska file](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) is copied into a `.mov` first and named after the original. A file the [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) converts is recorded the same way.
47	
48	A tool call never asks, so where the app would offer to convert a file with ffmpeg, this answers with the reason instead. Convert it from the app's window, or set Frame Job to always convert.
49	
50	It's refused when nothing exists at `path`, or when the file can't be read. A file whose path is already on the list changes nothing, and the answer says so. The step is called "Add Media".
51	
52	## `add_media`
53	
54	Adds a media entry from a description you supply, with no reading of the file. Use `import_media` unless you're replaying a project's own JSON. Frame Job has no menu item for this tool, because reading the file is the app's job.
55	
56	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `descriptor` | object | Yes | The entry to add, as below. |
59	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
60	| `project` | string | No | The project to add it to. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
61	
62	The descriptor is an element of `media` from `get_project`, without its `id`. Only `path` is required by name.
63	
64	| Key | What it is | Default |
65	| --- | --- | --- |
66	| `path` | The file. A leading `~` is expanded. | |
67	| `bookmark` | A base64 file bookmark. | None |
68	| `kind` | `video`, `audio`, `image` or `lut`. | `video` |
69	| `duration` | The length, in ticks. | 0 |
70	| `width`, `height` | The size in pixels. A file with pixels needs both. | 0 |
71	| `fps` | The frame rate, as `[numerator, denominator]`. | `[30, 1]` |
72	| `has_video` | Whether it has a picture. | On for `video` and `image` |
73	| `has_audio` | Whether it has sound. | On for `audio` |
74	| `has_alpha` | Whether it has an alpha channel. | Off |
75	| `original` | `{path, bookmark?}`: the file a `.mov` copy or conversion was made from. | None |
76	| `color` | A video file's Camera Log, as `set_media_color` takes it, plus `detected`, and `pq`, a PQ file's `{file?, from?, peak?}` as `get_project` shows it. | None |
77	| `cursor` | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`: the cursor file recorded beside a video, with `in_picture` true when the movie's own picture already shows the pointer. Both `path` and `in_picture` are required, and it's for a video with a picture only. | None |
78	
79	It answers `ok: true`, `media` (the new id), `path` and the `project` summary.
80	
81	An unknown key is refused by name, and so is a value of the wrong shape. A picture with no width or height, a video with a frame-rate term of 0, an empty path and a negative duration are all refused. A `color` that `set_media_color` wouldn't take is refused too. A path already on the list changes nothing.
82	
83	## `relink_media`
84	
85	Points a media entry at a file that moved, as [the Relink… sheet](/projects/relink-media/) and the Media tab's row menu do. `get_project`'s `missing_media` names the entries that need this.
86	
87	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
88	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
89	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
90	| `path` | string | Yes | Where the file is now. |
91	| `bookmark` | string | No | A base64 file bookmark. Leave it out and one is made for you, so the next move is followed automatically. |
92	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
93	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
94	
95	The new file is read as `import_media` reads one, and the entry takes its duration, size, frame rate and audio, video and alpha flags. What happens to the rest is on [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/#what-a-relink-keeps):
96	
97	- A clip running past the end of a shorter file is shortened to end with it. One that starts past the new end keeps a single frame.
98	- Camera Log and an HDR10 peak are kept.
99	- Saved speech is held to the new file, and forgotten when the new file has no sound.
100	- The cursor file beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the old one stays as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the entry's cursor file is cleared.
101	- A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a `.mov` first, and a file the ffmpeg step converts is recorded the same way. Either becomes the entry's new `original`, and any other file clears it.
102	
103	It answers `ok: true`, `media`, `path`, `kind`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_video`, `has_audio`, `has_alpha`, `original` when there is one, and the `project` summary.
104	
105	It's refused when no media has that id, when nothing exists at `path`, when the file can't be read, and for a file of another kind, such as a sound file for a video entry. The step is called "Relink Media".
106	
107	## `remove_media`
108	
109	Removes a media entry from the project, as [**Remove** in the Media tab's row menu](/projects/remove-media/) does. The file on disk isn't touched.
110	
111	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
112	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
113	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
114	| `with_clips` | boolean | No | Remove the clips using it as well, including those inside nests. For a LUT, clear the looks and Camera Log conversions that name it instead. Default `false`. |
115	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
116	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
117	
118	A nest clip isn't a user of the file, so it stays even when clips inside it go. Any [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) setting that listens to the file is cleared.
119	
120	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary.
121	
122	It's refused while clips use the file and `with_clips` isn't `true`, naming the clips. A LUT in use as a look or a Camera Log is refused the same way, naming what uses it. The step is called "Remove Media".
123	
124	## `consolidate_media`
125	
126	Copies every file the project references into `media/` inside the `.framejob` package and relinks the project at the copies, as [**File ▸ Consolidate Media…**](/projects/consolidate-media/) does. Afterwards the package is the whole edit. It can be moved or archived and still open with the original footage deleted.
127	
128	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
129	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
130	| `project` | string | No | The project to consolidate. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
131	
132	It copies as many bytes as the footage weighs, so it can take a while, and it has no **Cancel**. Frame Job's window doesn't respond until it's done. A recording's cursor file is copied beside its movie.
133	
134	Files already inside are left alone, and missing files are reported rather than guessed at. A file that can't be copied keeps pointing at the original, so the project always still opens.
135	
136	It answers `ok: true`, `copied`, `bytes`, `directory`, `summary`, `failures` and `missing` when there are any, and the `project` summary. When every file it can find is already inside, it answers `copied: 0`, `directory`, `missing`, a `note`, and the summary, and makes no step.
137	
138	It's refused when the project has never been saved, so call `save_project` with a path first, when the project references no media files, and when nothing could be copied. The step is called "Consolidate Media".
139	
140	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first.
141	
142	## `set_media_color`
143	
144	Sets how a video file's camera log footage is converted to Rec. 709, as the Media tab's [Camera Log popup](/hdr/camera-log/) does, and where a PQ file's highlights roll off to white, as its [HDR10 Peak field](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) does.
145	
146	Every clip of the file and its reverse follow the setting. It's converted before the chroma key and every grade, and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) keeps it.
147	
148	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
149	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
150	| `media` | integer | Yes | The video's media id, or a PQ still's for `peak` alone. |
151	| `color` | object or null | Yes | What to set, as below. `null` clears it, but the key must be there. |
152	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
153	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
154	
155	`color` is one of these:
156	
157	| `color` | What it does |
158	| --- | --- |
159	| `{log, gamut?}` | Converts with a built-in curve. |
160	| `{lut}` | Converts with an imported `.cube`, named by its media id. [`import_media`](#import_media) it first. See [Camera log from your own LUT](/hdr/log-luts/). |
161	| `{peak}` | A PQ file's peak, a whole number of cd/m² from 1 to 10,000. |
162	| `log` or `lut` beside `peak` | Both at once. |
163	| `null` | No conversion, which shows the log picture, and no peak override. |
164	
165	The curves, and the gamuts each takes. An absent `gamut` means the first one listed:
166	
167	| `log` | The curve | `gamut` |
168	| --- | --- | --- |
169	| `apple_log` | Apple Log | `bt2020` |
170	| `apple_log2` | Apple Log 2 | `apple_wide_gamut` |
171	| `slog3` | S-Log3 | `s_gamut3_cine`, `s_gamut3` |
172	| `vlog` | V-Log | `v_gamut` |
173	| `canon_log2` | Canon Log 2 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |
174	| `canon_log3` | Canon Log 3 | `cinema_gamut`, `bt2020` |
175	
176	An Apple Log or Apple Log 2 file is set at import, and `get_project` shows `detected: true` in the file's `media[].color`.
177	
178	Import reads a PQ file's own peak into `media[].color.pq`, as `{file, from}`: MaxCLL, or else the mastering display's maximum. When the file names neither, `pq` is `{}`, which means 1,000. `peak` overrides that reading.
179	
180	:::caution
181	`color` replaces the Camera Log and the peak together, so send both to keep both. `null` clears both, and the peak goes back to the file's own reading.
182	:::
183	
184	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary. The step is called "PQ Peak" when `color` holds only `peak`, and "Camera Log" otherwise.
185	
186	It's refused:
187	
188	- on an audio file or a LUT
189	- on a picture, unless it's a PQ still and `color` is `peak` alone
190	- for a `peak` on a file that isn't PQ, or outside 1 to 10,000
191	- for a `color` with none of `log`, `lut` and `peak`
192	- for `log` and `lut` together
193	- for a `gamut` without a `log`, or one its curve doesn't take
194	- for a `lut` that doesn't name a LUT in the project
195	- for `detected` or `pq`, which only import writes
196	
197	## `set_media_speech`
198	
199	Saves where a file's speech is. [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) ducks the mix by these spans, and [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) reads them too.
200	
201	Setting **Duck by** to **Speech** in the Sound sub-tab's **Ducking** section writes them from the file's detected speech, and so does [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) with `duck.mode` set to speech. Call this only to give spans of your own.
202	
203	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
204	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
205	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
206	| `spans` | array of `[start, end]` pairs | Yes | Where the speech is, in ticks of the file played forward, sorted, with each end excluded. An empty list means the file has no speech. |
207	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
208	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
209	
210	It answers `ok: true`, `media` and the `project` summary, and `get_project` shows the spans as `media[].speech`. Spans equal to what the file already has change nothing. The step is called "Speech Spans".
211	
212	It's refused:
213	
214	- on a file with no sound
215	- for a span that starts before 0, ends at or before its start, or ends past the file's duration
216	- for spans out of order or overlapping. Touching is fine.
217	- past 100,000 spans
218

1	---
2	title: "Tools: adding clips"
3	description: The agent tools that place media, titles, shapes, adjustment clips and backgrounds on the timeline, with every argument, answer and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools put new clips on the timeline. Three place a media file, three make a clip with no source, and two make a backdrop on a new track of its own.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['add_clip', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
12	/>
13	
14	## What the tools share
15	
16	Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true`, `new_clips` (the ids it made), `new_tracks` when it made a track, and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
17	
18	Times and lengths are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. A negative `at` is taken as 0. Colours are four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
19	
20	**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
21	
22	**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
23	
24	**The overlap rule** stops a placement that breaks it. A clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip, because an overlap is a transition. A new clip that overlaps the clip before it and has no transition gets a cross dissolve.
25	
26	**A locked track** doesn't stop these tools, apart from `insert_clip`. Locks hold back gestures in the window and what a timeline-wide shift may touch.
27	
28	## `add_clip`
29	
30	Places a whole media file as one clip, as [dragging a Media-tab row onto a track](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) does.
31	
32	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. `get_project` lists them. |
35	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. `import_media` returns one. |
36	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the clip starts on the timeline, in ticks. |
37	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to place it in. |
38	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
39	
40	The clip starts at source time 0 and runs the media's whole length, rounded down to whole frames so it never outruns the file. Trim it afterwards with [`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start) and [`trim_end`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_end). A picture with no length of its own runs 5 seconds.
41	
42	It's given Fit scale when the project's `fit_new_clips` is on, which it is by default, and the source is bigger than the canvas.
43	
44	It's refused when it would break the overlap rule. A media shorter than a frame or with no duration can't be placed, and neither can a LUT, which is applied as a [look](/mcp/tools-set-video/). The step is called "Add Clip".
45	
46	## `insert_clip`
47	
48	The insert edit, as [**Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file) or <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It makes room for the whole media at `at`, so nothing is covered.
49	
50	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
51	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
52	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
53	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
54	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to insert, in ticks. |
55	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to insert in. |
56	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
57	
58	In one step:
59	
60	1. The clip `at` falls inside on `track` is split.
61	2. Every unlocked track opens by the media's length. Clips starting at or after `at` move later, and so do markers at or after it.
62	3. The media lands in the hole.
63	
64	Only the destination track is cut. A clip straddling `at` on another track stays whole, which is what keeps a music bed unbroken. The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at `at` too and paired with it.
65	
66	It's refused when `track` is locked, because the room can't be made there, and when a step of the edit is refused, in that step's own words. A media `add_clip` can't place can't be inserted either. The step is called "Insert".
67	
68	## `overwrite_clip`
69	
70	The overwrite edit, as [**Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#overwrite-with-a-file) or <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It takes the room instead of making it.
71	
72	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
73	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
74	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
75	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
76	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to overwrite, in ticks. |
77	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to overwrite in. |
78	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
79	
80	The span the media needs is cleared on `track` alone: cut at both ends, and whatever is left inside removed. Nothing shifts, so the cut's length and every other track stay as they are.
81	
82	The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at the same bounds and paired. The partner's middle piece stays, unlinked.
83	
84	The named track is cleared even when it's locked. It's refused when the clip can't be placed once the span is clear, and a media `add_clip` can't place can't be used here either. The step is called "Overwrite".
85	
86	## `add_text_clip`
87	
88	Adds a text clip, a title, as the [**Add Text**](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#add-a-text-clip) button does. It has no source, so it can be any length. Style it afterwards with `set_text` and place it with `set_video`.
89	
90	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
91	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
92	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
93	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
94	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
95	| `text` | object or string | No | A plain string is the words. An object is a `set_text` patch merged over the Title preset. Default: the preset's own placeholder, "Title". |
96	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
97	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
98	
99	A new clip is the Title preset: 72 px white Source Sans 3 Bold, centred. An object can set anything [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) can, including `content`, `font`, `size`, `color`, `align`, `valign`, `outline`, `backdrop`, `width`, `animation`, `case`, `words` and `word_style`. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
100	
101	```json
102	{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "text": "Chapter one" }
103	{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "duration": 1200000,
104	  "text": { "content": "Chapter one", "size": 96, "align": "left" } }
105	```
106	
107	It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown key or a bad value in the patch, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Add Text".
108	
109	## `add_shape_clip`
110	
111	Adds a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow drawn over the video, as [**Add Shape**](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip) does. Like text, it has no source and can be any length. [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) changes it afterwards and `set_video` places it.
112	
113	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
114	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
115	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
116	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
117	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
118	| `shape` | object or string | No | A plain string is a kind: `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line` or `arrow`. An object is a `set_shape` patch merged over the default rectangle. |
119	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
120	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
121	
122	Leave out `shape` for the default: a 320×120 rectangle, outlined with no fill. An object can set `kind`, `width`, `height`, `stroke`, `fill`, `radius`, `arrow_start`, `arrow_end`, `from`, `to` and `gradient`.
123	
124	A rounded rectangle is a rectangle with a `radius`, not a kind of its own. An arrow is created with its head on, so pass `arrow_end: false` for a bare diagonal. A box bigger than the canvas gets Fit scale when `fit_new_clips` is on, as oversized footage does.
125	
126	It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown kind, key or value, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Add Shape".
127	
128	## `add_adjustment_clip`
129	
130	Adds an adjustment clip, as [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) does. It has no picture of its own. While it lasts, it grades everything drawn behind it: every lower track and the canvas background, never a track in front.
131	
132	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
133	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
134	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
135	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
136	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
137	| `scope` | integer | No | Answers that this has no meaning inside a nest. |
138	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
139	
140	Grade it with [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/): `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, `qualifier`, and the point filters (sepia, noir, vignette and invert). Its `opacity` is the grade's strength. On a track cut by a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) it grades only inside the matte, and on a matte track it does nothing.
141	
142	It's refused:
143	
144	- inside a nest, whether you pass `scope` or a nest is open
145	- in any transition or overlap. Fade it with `opacity` instead.
146	
147	Later, `set_video` gives an error for blur, sharpen, pixelate or a blend mode on it. The step is called "Add Adjustment Clip".
148	
149	## `add_background`
150	
151	Puts a backdrop on a new back-most track, starting at 0 and running the timeline's length, as [**Clip ▸ Add Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/) does. The clip is named "Background".
152	
153	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
154	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
155	| `color` | array of four numbers | No | The plate's colour, as `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. White when left out. |
156	| `media` | integer | No | A media id to show instead of a colour. `import_media` adds a file. |
157	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default: the whole timeline's length, and never less than one frame. |
158	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
159	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
160	
161	With no arguments it's a canvas-sized white rectangle, which is what the menu's **Solid Color** row sends. It's white because the canvas is already black, so a black plate would appear to do nothing. A full-canvas gradient is this clip with [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/)'s `gradient` after it.
162	
163	With `media` the picture goes there at Fill scale, where `add_clip` would Fit it, because a plate that leaves the canvas showing down one side has failed. A video plate stops where its file does, whatever `duration` says. A picture runs the timeline, or for `duration` when you give one.
164	
165	It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.
166	
167	These are errors, and nothing is added:
168	
169	- `media` and `color` together
170	- a `duration` under one frame
171	- a media with no pictures, such as a sound file
172	- a colour that isn't four numbers from 0 to 1
173	
174	The step is called "Add Background".
175	
176	## `add_blurred_background`
177	
178	The screencast backdrop, as [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) does. It copies a clip onto a new back-most track at the same start, duration, speed and source window, so the two play exactly the same frames.
179	
180	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
181	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
182	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. `get_project` lists them. |
183	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
184	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
185	
186	The copy is named "Blurred Background". It's scaled to fill the canvas, centred, uncropped, blended normally and blurred at full strength.
187	
188	Its sound is off, or the mix would play one recording twice. It drops the original's ducking, because a copy keeping it would duck the whole mix, and it drops its transition, actions and label too.
189	
190	It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.
191	
192	These are errors, and nothing is added:
193	
194	- a nest clip, whose copy would come out sharp
195	- a source with no pixel size, such as a text clip or a sound-only clip
196	- a clip with no video properties
197	
198	The step is called "Add Blurred Background".
199

1	---
2	title: "Tools: moving and trimming"
3	description: The agent tools that move clips, trim their edges, slip their source, roll a cut and switch a clip's picture or sound, with every argument and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools change where a clip sits and what it shows. They name clips by id, so read them from `get_project` first.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'slip', 'roll', 'set_enabled']} />
11	
12	## What the tools share
13	
14	Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true` and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
15	
16	**Clamped, not refused.** Most of these hold a time to what the clip's source allows and do as much as they can. Read the clip back to see where it landed. When the limits leave nothing to do, the answer says "*Step* made no change", and no undo step is made.
17	
18	**Times** are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
19	
20	**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
21	
22	**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
23	
24	**Linked pairs.** After [`detach_audio`](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/), a picture and its sound move together. The partner comes along only when it's on an unlocked track. A lock on a named clip's own track doesn't stop these tools.
25	
26	**A boolean** may also be sent as `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`.
27	
28	## `move_clip`
29	
30	Shifts clips along the timeline, and optionally onto another track, as [dragging a clip](/editing/move-clips/) does.
31	
32	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
35	| `delta` | integer | Yes | How far to shift, in ticks. Negative moves earlier. |
36	| `track` | integer | No | The destination track for the first clip. The first clip is the one on the back-most track, then the earliest. Leave it out to stay on the current tracks. |
37	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clips are in. |
38	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
39	
40	Several clips keep their relative track offsets, so a selection spanning two tracks lands two tracks apart.
41	
42	Starts stop at 0. It's the earliest clip that stops there, linked partners included, and the rest keep their distance from it.
43	
44	A linked pair moves together in time, but only the clips you name change track. So you can drop a sound half onto a track of its own while its picture stays.
45	
46	It's refused:
47	
48	- when the destination breaks the overlap rule: a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip
49	- when a clip would land off either end of the track list
50	
51	A clip that gains an overlap with the clip before it, and has no transition, gains a `cross_dissolve`. The step is called "Move Clip".
52	
53	## `trim_start`
54	
55	Moves a clip's start, as [dragging its left edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>W</kbd> does. The content stays in place: the source's in point advances by the same amount, so nothing after the new start shifts.
56	
57	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
58	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
59	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
60	| `to` | integer | Yes | The new start, in ticks. |
61	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this clip's edge without its linked partner's, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). The timeline does this for a dragged sound. Default `false`. |
62	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
63	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
64	
65	It stops at the source's own beginning and one frame short of the clip's end, because a clip is at least one frame long.
66	
67	On a linked pair, the other half's start follows when it was the same as this clip's.
68	
69	Timed words stay on the speech they time, and a graphic's own clock moves with the edge. Actions stay where they are in the clip. See [What a trim keeps](/editing/trimming/#what-a-trim-keeps).
70	
71	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after the new start can change. The start is held where the clip still fits its media.
72	
73	It's refused when the new start would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Trim Start".
74	
75	## `trim_end`
76	
77	Moves a clip's end, as [dragging its right edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>E</kbd> does.
78	
79	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
80	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
81	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
82	| `to` | integer | Yes | The new end, in ticks. |
83	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this clip's edge without its linked partner's, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Default `false`. |
84	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
85	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
86	
87	It stops at the last frame the source has left after the in point, and one frame after the clip's start.
88	
89	On a linked pair, the other half's end follows when it was the same as this clip's.
90	
91	It's refused when the new end would break the overlap rule. The step is called "Trim End".
92	
93	## `slip`
94	
95	Slides the source under a fixed clip, as [<kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-dragging a clip's body](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) does. What the clip shows changes, and where it sits doesn't, so nothing downstream moves.
96	
97	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
98	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
99	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
100	| `delta` | integer | Yes | How far to slide the source, in timeline ticks. The source moves by `delta` times the clip's speed. Positive shows later material. |
101	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
102	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
103	
104	The slide stops so the window stays inside the media. A [freeze clip](/speed/freeze-frame/) moves the frame it holds instead, and stops one frame short of the file's end.
105	
106	A linked partner on an unlocked track slips too, by whichever of the two can move less, so the sound stays on its picture. Actions don't move.
107	
108	Any clip other than a media or freeze clip is an error. The step is called "Slip".
109	
110	## `roll`
111	
112	Moves a hard cut between two clips, as [<kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-dragging a clip's edge](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) does. This clip's start and the end of the clip before it both become `to`. One grows by exactly what the other loses, and the pair's outer edges and total length don't move.
113	
114	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
115	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
116	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to the right of the cut. |
117	| `to` | integer | Yes | Where the cut moves to, in ticks. |
118	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this cut without rolling the linked partner's. Default `false`. |
119	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
120	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
121	
122	The clip before is the one on the same track that ends exactly at this clip's start.
123	
124	The cut stops so each clip keeps a frame and neither asks for source it doesn't have. On a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/) it's held where the clip still fits its media.
125	
126	The linked half of a pair rolls its own cut too, when it starts at the same time and has a hard cut of its own there.
127	
128	It's refused when no clip on the track ends where this one begins, with "no clip on track … ends where clip … begins". That covers a gap and an overlap. An overlap is a transition, so use [`set_transition_duration`](/mcp/tools-transitions/) to change its length. The step is called "Roll".
129	
130	## `set_enabled`
131	
132	Turns one clip's picture or sound on or off, the two halves [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) flips. A half that's off adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and the clip stays where it is.
133	
134	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
135	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
136	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
137	| `video` | boolean | No | Show this clip's picture. Left out, it stays as it is. |
138	| `audio` | boolean | No | Play this clip's sound. Left out, it stays as it is. |
139	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
140	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
141	
142	It's refused when neither `video` nor `audio` is given. A value the clip already has changes nothing. The step is called "Clip Enabled".
143

1	---
2	title: "Tools: projects and history"
3	description: The agent tools that open, make, save, close and read a project, and walk its undo history, with every argument, answer and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools work on whole projects: opening, making, saving and closing them, reading one back, and stepping through its undo history. None of them takes `scope`, because none of them edits inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'save_project', 'close_project', 'get_project', 'undo', 'redo']}
12	/>
13	
14	Every tool takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. A path that names no open project is refused, and so is a call with no project open at all, which is told to call `open_project` or `new_project` first. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/) for how times are written, and [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) for the short `project` summary most answers carry.
15	
16	## `open_project`
17	
18	Opens a project and shows its window, as [double-clicking a file](/projects/open-a-project/) does. It takes a `.framejob` package, or any movie, sound file or picture. A movie, sound file or picture [becomes a new untitled project](/projects/start-a-project/) sized and rated to it, with the file as the first clip on track 1.
19	
20	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
22	| `path` | string | Yes | The file to open, as an absolute path or one starting with `~`. |
23	| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |
24	
25	It answers the opened project's `project` summary, with `missing_media` in that summary when a file has gone. If the file is already open, Frame Job brings that project forward and answers `already_open: true` with its summary. That includes a movie already open as an untitled project.
26	
27	It's refused when:
28	
29	- nothing exists at `path`
30	- the file can't be read, or doesn't open as a Frame Job project
31	- you're opening the same file in a window and that open hasn't finished after 30 seconds. Call it again once the window is up.
32	
33	A tool call never asks a question, so a file that would normally bring up the [ffmpeg offer](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) is treated as if you'd declined it.
34	
35	## `new_project`
36	
37	Makes a blank 1920×1080, 30 fps project and shows its window, as [**File ▸ New Project**](/projects/start-a-project/#start-a-blank-project) does. Change its size and rate afterwards with [`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
38	
39	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
40	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
41	| `path` | string | No | Where to save it straight away, such as `~/Movies/Cut.framejob`. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Without a path the project stays an untitled draft until `save_project`. |
42	| `project` | string | No | Accepted, and makes no difference, because this call doesn't act on an open project. |
43	
44	It answers the new project's `project` summary, and `saved`, the full path, when you gave one.
45	
46	A path another open project holds is refused and nothing is created. `close_project` closes that project first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced.
47	
48	## `new_project_from_range`
49	
50	Opens a stretch of the top-level timeline as a new project, moved to start at 0, as [**File ▸ New Project from Range…**](/projects/new-project-from-range/) does with the in/out range. The project you take it from doesn't change and gets no undo step.
51	
52	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
53	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
54	| `from` | integer | Yes | Where the range starts on the timeline, in ticks. It's rounded to a frame, and a negative time is taken as 0. |
55	| `to` | integer | Yes | Where the range ends on the timeline, in ticks. The frame at `to` isn't kept. It must be after `from`. |
56	| `path` | string | No | Where to save the new project first. `.framejob` is added when it's missing, and nothing may exist there yet. Without it the project opens untitled, with unsaved changes, named "*name* (range)". |
57	| `project` | string | No | The project to take the range from. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
58	
59	What's kept follows the sheet:
60	
61	- A clip across an edge is cut there, on every track, as [`split`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/) would cut it. Locked tracks are cut too.
62	- A transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end.
63	- Markers inside the range are kept and moved with it.
64	- Media nothing kept plays is left out.
65	- Each kept file's caches come along, so nothing is analysed again, and so do the graphics the kept clips draw, with every font and picture. [What comes with it](/projects/new-project-from-range/#what-comes-with-it) has the list.
66	- Media files are never copied. The new project points at the same files.
67	
68	It answers `project`, the new project's summary, `carried` with the `files`, `bytes` and `seconds` that came along, and `saved`, the path, when you gave one. The new project opens in front, so later calls with no `project` reach it. Name it by its path once it has one.
69	
70	It's refused:
71	
72	- while a nest is open. Call `set_scope` with no arguments first.
73	- when `to` isn't after `from`, once both are on the frame grid
74	- for a path another open project holds, or where anything already exists
75	- for a nest clip across either edge, because a nest clip has no in point and would replay from its start
76	- when nothing plays in the range
77	- when an edge would leave a transition inside the range too long for what's left of its clip. Move that edge further from the transition.
78	
79	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first when the call names a `path`.
80	
81	## `save_project`
82	
83	Saves the project, as [**File ▸ Save**](/projects/save-and-revert/#save-a-project) does, and answers only once the package is on disk.
84	
85	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
86	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
87	| `path` | string | The first time | Where to write the `.framejob` package. `.framejob` is added when it's missing. Giving a path always writes there, as Save As does, unless it's the project's own file, which is a plain save. |
88	| `project` | string | No | The project to save. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
89	
90	A project needs a `path` the first time, whether it came from `new_project` with no path or from a movie opened as a project. After that, leave it out and the project is written back to its own file.
91	
92	It answers `saved`, the full path, and the `project` summary.
93	
94	It's refused when a project that has never been saved has no `path`, and for a path another open project holds. `close_project` closes that one first. A path a window is still opening is refused the same way. A file on disk that no open project holds is replaced. A save that takes more than 120 seconds answers that it timed out.
95	
96	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you first.
97	
98	## `close_project`
99	
100	Closes a project and its window, as [**File ▸ Close**](/projects/save-and-revert/#close-a-project) (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) does. It never writes the package, so call `save_project` first to keep your changes.
101	
102	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
103	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
104	| `discard` | boolean | No | Close even with unsaved changes, losing them. Default `false`. |
105	| `project` | string | No | The project to close. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
106	
107	It answers `ok: true`, `closed` (the project's name), `path` (null for a blank project never saved) and `discarded_changes`, which says whether unsaved changes went with it. A later call naming that path is refused, because it's no longer open.
108	
109	It's refused when the window has a sheet open, whatever `discard` says, and when `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes` and `discard` isn't `true`.
110	
111	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call this tool, because closing the project would close its own conversation.
112	
113	## `get_project`
114	
115	Answers the whole project as JSON, plus what the app holds outside it: the playhead, the selection and the in/out range. Read it first, because every other tool names things by the ids it reports. [Read the project: get_project](/mcp/get-project/) goes through it in full.
116	
117	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
118	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
119	| `project` | string | No | The project to read. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
120	
121	Its answer holds:
122	
123	| Key | What it is |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| `project` | The project itself, including `canvas`, `media`, `tracks`, `clips`, `markers`, `nests` and `next_id`. |
126	| `path`, `name` | Where the project is, or null, and what it's called. |
127	| `unsaved_changes` | Whether it has changes not yet saved. |
128	| `duration`, `playhead` | Its length and the playhead, in ticks. |
129	| `selection` | The selected clip ids. |
130	| `in_out_range` | `start` and `end`, in ticks. Only there when a range is set. |
131	| `scope` | The open nest's id, or null at the timeline. With a nest open, `scope_clip` and `scope_path` come with it. |
132	| `missing_media` | The ids of media whose file has gone. Only there when one has. |
133	| `graphics` | Every module in the package, with its revision, whether it compiles, and the clips it draws. |
134	| `note` | A reminder of how to read the rest. |
135	
136	While a nest is open, `project` is that nest seen as a project. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
137	
138	## `undo`
139	
140	Undoes one step, as [**Edit ▸ Undo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) does. Every tool that edits makes exactly one step, so one `undo` walks back exactly one call. The history is the project's, so a step you made by hand counts as well.
141	
142	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
143	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
144	| `project` | string | No | The project to undo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
145	
146	It answers `ok: true`, `undone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.
147	
148	It's refused when there's nothing to undo. The tools on [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/) make no step, so they can't be undone.
149	
150	## `redo`
151	
152	Redoes one undone step, as [**Edit ▸ Redo**](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/#undo-and-redo) (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) does. Any new edit clears what there was to redo, as it does in the app.
153	
154	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
155	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
156	| `project` | string | No | The project to redo in. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
157	
158	It answers `ok: true`, `redone` (the name of the step), `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the `project` summary.
159	
160	It's refused when there's nothing to redo.
161

2	title: "Tools: playhead, range and selection"
3	description: The agent tools that move the playhead, set the in/out range, select clips and open a nest, none of which is an edit.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These four tools change what the app is looking at, never the project. They make no undo step and leave the project untouched, so `undo` can't reverse them. `get_project` reads all of them back.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />
11	
12	Times are in ticks, 600,000 per second, and each is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). Every tool here takes an optional `project`, the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
13	
14	## `set_playhead`
15	
16	Moves the playhead and seeks the preview, as [clicking the ruler or a transport key](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) does.
17	
18	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| `t` | integer | Yes | The time to move to, in ticks. A negative time goes to 0. |
21	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
22	
23	It answers `ok: true`, `playhead` (the time it landed on) and the `project` summary.
24	
25	`split`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker` use this time when they aren't given one. While a [nest](/mcp/nests/) is open, `t` is measured from the nest's own start.
26	
27	## `set_range`
28	
29	Sets or clears the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), as **Mark ▸ Set In** (<kbd>I</kbd>), **Mark ▸ Set Out** (<kbd>O</kbd>) and **Mark ▸ Clear Range** (<kbd>⌥X</kbd>) do.
30	
31	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| `start` | integer | No | The In point, in ticks. Left out, it keeps the range's current In, or 0 when there's no range. |
34	| `end` | integer | No | The Out point, in ticks. Left out, it keeps the range's current Out, or the project's end when there's no range. |
35	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
36	
37	Call it with neither bound to clear the range. A negative time is taken as 0.
38	
39	It answers `ok: true`, `in_out_range` (`start` and `end`, or null when the range is cleared) and the `project` summary.
40	
41	It's refused when the end isn't after the start. [`export`](/mcp/export/) with `range: "in_out"` writes only this span, and `get_project` reports it as `in_out_range`.
42	
43	## `set_selection`
44	
45	Selects clips, as [clicking one](/timeline/selecting-clips/) in the timeline or on the canvas, or **Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>), does. The canvas handles, crop mode and every inspector pane act on the selection, so this puts the app into the state you want to look at.
46	
47	You don't need it to edit. The editing tools take their own `clip` or `clips`.
48	
49	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
50	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
51	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clip ids to select, replacing the selection. Leave it out, or pass an empty array, to select nothing. |
52	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
53	
54	It answers `ok: true`, `selection` (the selected ids, in order) and the `project` summary.
55	
56	An id that isn't a clip is refused by name. With a nest open, ids mean clips inside that nest, so a clip on the timeline can't be selected until you come back out with `set_scope`.
57	
58	## `set_scope`
59	
60	Opens a nest so the app is looking inside it, or comes back out, as [double-clicking a nest clip](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest), **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>) and **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>) do.
61	
62	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
63	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
64	| `clip` | integer | No | The nest clip to open. This is the precise choice: it names the nest and the start that times inside are measured from, and it works at any depth. |
65	| `nest` | integer | No | The nest to open, by id, as `get_project` lists them under `nests`. A clip on the timeline must show it. Where two clips do, the earliest is entered, and a tie goes to the lower id. |
66	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
67	
68	Pass `clip` or `nest`, not both. Pass neither to come back out to the timeline. The call names where to be, not a step to take, so it means the same thing from any depth.
69	
70	While a nest is open:
71	
72	- `get_project` reports the nest's own tracks, clips and canvas, and [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) draws it. This is the only way to see what an edit inside a nest did.
73	- An edit lands inside the nest, unless its own `scope` says otherwise or it belongs to the whole project, as a change to the [media list](/mcp/tools-media/) does. So open the nest first, and clear it when you're done.
74	
75	Going in maps the playhead to the nest's own time and selects nothing. Coming out maps it back and selects the nest clip you opened.
76	
77	You don't need this tool to edit inside a nest. An edit tool's `scope` argument works from wherever the window is looking. [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/) covers both ways.
78	
79	It answers `ok: true`, `scope` (the nest's id, or null at the timeline), `scope_clip` and `scope_path` with a nest open, `playhead`, and the `project` summary.
80	
81	It's refused when:
82	
83	- both `clip` and `nest` are given
84	- no clip has that id, at the timeline or in any nest
85	- the clip doesn't show a nest
86	- no nest has that id
87	- no clip on the timeline shows that nest. Name the nest clip with `clip`, or send the edit with `scope`.
